## Evaporation of condensates by diffusion (`type: evaporation`) {#sec-ch06-evaporation}

### Summary

An evaporation reaction turns one condensed species into gases at a rate set by vapor diffusion to the particles and
by how far the gas is below saturation. It is one-way: condensation is handled by the phase equilibrium of
@sec-ch04, and evaporation only lets condensate that sits in subsaturated air return to the gas.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** $r = \kappa\, c_p\, \eta$ with $\kappa = 12 D v_m / d^2$, @eq-ch06-evaporation-kappa.

**Data.** $T$ [K], $p$ [Pa], $c$ [$\mathrm{mol\,m^{-3}}$] in; $r$ [$\mathrm{mol\,m^{-3}\,s^{-1}}$] out.

**Placement.** Third evaluator of `Kinetics.forward`.

**Activation.** `type: evaporation`, `form: diffusion` (the default); saturation from the `formula` keys.

**Guarantee / limits.** $\eta \ge 0$: never condenses.

**Evidence.** See the Tests layer.
:::

Local symbols: $D$, vapor diffusivity [$\mathrm{m^2\,s^{-1}}$]; $v_m$, molar volume of the condensate
[$\mathrm{m^3\,mol^{-1}}$]; $d$, particle diameter [m]; $c_p$, condensate concentration [$\mathrm{mol\,m^{-3}}$];
$\eta$, saturation deficit [units of the product of gas concentrations]; $K$, saturation product.

Defaults: `diff_c` $2 \times 10^{-5}\,\mathrm{m^2\,s^{-1}}$, `diff_T` 1.75, `diff_P` $-1$, `vm`
$1.8 \times 10^{-5}\,\mathrm{m^3\,mol^{-1}}$, `diameter` $10^{-2}$ m, `Tref` 300 K, `Pref` $10^5$ Pa.

### Derivation

The diffusivity scales as

$$
D = D_0 \left(\frac{T}{T_{\mathrm{ref}}}\right)^{a_T} \left(\frac{p}{p_{\mathrm{ref}}}\right)^{a_p},
$$

with $D_0$, $a_T$, $a_p$ the YAML keys `diff_c`, `diff_T`, `diff_P`. The rate coefficient and the rate are

$$
\begin{aligned}
\kappa &= \frac{12\, D\, v_m}{d^2},\\
r &= \kappa\, c_p\, \eta .
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch06-evaporation-kappa}

For one gas product, $\eta = \max(K - c_v, 0)$, with $K$ the saturation concentration from the vapor-pressure
formula of @sec-ch02 divided by $\mathcal R T$. For two gas products the code replaces the deficit by the extent $x$
that brings the products to equilibrium, $(c_1 + x)(c_2 + x) = K$. Other stoichiometries use the general surface
extent of `EvaporationExtent`. @eq-ch06-evaporation-kappa is computed in `forward`
({{< code src/kinetics/evaporation.cpp EvaporationImpl::forward >}}); the factor $c_p$ is applied in
`forward_with_rate_constants` ({{< code src/kinetics/kinetics.cpp KineticsImpl::forward_with_rate_constants >}}).
The origin of the factor 12 is not drafted yet.

### Numerical method

The two-product extent is the positive root of a quadratic, written as
$x = 2(K - c_1 c_2) / (c_1 + c_2 + \sqrt{(c_1 - c_2)^2 + 4K})$ so that no difference of large terms occurs. Columns
that are already supersaturated, including an infinite product, have their concentrations zeroed before the
extent is formed, so no infinity reaches the gradient. The general extent is an autograd function with an implicit
first derivative ({{< code src/kinetics/evaporation_extent.cpp EvaporationExtent::forward >}}).

The figure of $\eta$ against $c_v$ is not provided: the figure module is not written yet.

: Code map of evaporation. {#tbl-ch06-evaporation-code}

Refused at setup: a reversible reaction; a coefficient that is not finite and positive; custom `orders`; more or
fewer than one condensed reactant, or a condensed reactant with a coefficient other than 1; a condensate as a
product; a mixed-reactant reaction without explicit phases.

`minT` and `maxT` are stored twice per evaporation reaction: once by `NucleationOptionsImpl::from_yaml`
({{< code src/thermo/nucleation.cpp NucleationOptionsImpl::from_yaml >}}), which the evaporation reader calls, and
again by `EvaporationOptionsImpl::from_yaml`. Verified: one reaction gives `minT == [0.0, 0.0]`. No reader of these
two lists was found in the kinetics sources, so the duplicate has no known effect.

|---|---|---|---|
| `test_evaporation_extent.py` | two-product rate is the extent | $10^{-10}$ rel. | not yet derived |
| `test_evaporation_extent.py` | rate derivative vs finite difference | $10^{-6}$ rel. | finite-difference step |
| `test_evaporation_general.py` | rate and Jacobian on CPU and CUDA agree | $10^{-12}$ abs. | not yet derived |
| `test_evaporation_inputs.py` | default diffusivity exponents | exact | structural |

: Tests of evaporation. {#tbl-ch06-evaporation-tests}

`test_evaporation_general.py` also checks atom conservation of an implicit step and convergence with the time step.
CUDA cases skip when no GPU is present.

### Limits

The factor 12 and the default diameter of 1 cm are taken as given; their source is missing evidence.
